meta.title: Daftar · Physics, Mathematics & Graph Memory
meta.coverage: Deep foundation-to-frontier study map; representative frontier coverage; catalogue entries are not individually verified proofs.

nodes.label: Typed knowledge graph
nodes.summary: Represent objects as stable vertices and relationships as named, directed edges. A graph stores assertions, not automatic truth.

nodes.label: Atomic concept and claim nodes
nodes.summary: Keep concepts, claims, formulas, sources, tasks, and artifacts distinguishable. Their identities must survive renaming.

nodes.label: Typed directed relations
nodes.summary: requires, supports, contradicts, derived_from, implements, and analogy have different semantics. Preserve direction and evidence.

nodes.label: Backlinks
nodes.summary: An incoming link is a reverse lookup of an existing edge, not a second independent source.

nodes.label: Unlinked mentions
nodes.summary: A matching name offers a link candidate. Resolve entity identity and meaning before treating it as a relation.

nodes.label: Entity identity and disambiguation
nodes.summary: Same label can denote different things; same object can have many labels. Stable IDs and explicit aliases reduce accidental merging.

nodes.label: Evidence provenance
nodes.summary: Keep source URL, exact version, date, section, access depth, and claim relationship separate from a summary.

nodes.label: Claim status and uncertainty
nodes.summary: Established theorem, approximation, measured result, preprint claim, disputed result, and open question must not share one undifferentiated confidence flag.

nodes.label: Content addressing
nodes.summary: Hash permitted source bytes or a canonical structured snapshot; a digest proves byte identity and does not prove truth.

nodes.label: Scope-first retrieval
nodes.summary: Select authorized observations before computing lexical statistics, graph propagation, and cache keys. The caller owns authentication.

nodes.label: Bitemporal evidence
nodes.summary: Separate when a fact applied from when it was recorded. Corrections append evidence rather than silently rewriting history.

nodes.label: Temporal validity intervals
nodes.summary: An observation is active when valid_from ≤ query_time < valid_until. Boundaries affect both graph edges and cached answers.

nodes.label: Immutable snapshots
nodes.summary: Write a content-addressed graph snapshot and then update its scope pointer. Keep original source identity with every derived artifact.

nodes.label: Event and decision ledger
nodes.summary: Record actual work, receipts, failures, owners, and next actions. An event is evidence of an operation, not a substitute for its artifact.

nodes.label: Write-ahead logs
nodes.summary: A transactional database can record changes before checkpointing state; its durability depends on the configured implementation.

nodes.label: SQLite transaction isolation
nodes.summary: Serialized writers and read snapshots are a possible next storage backend when filesystem snapshots become insufficient.

nodes.label: Result cache
nodes.summary: Reuse a derived result only when its query, snapshot, scope policy, algorithm, and time-dependent eligibility still match.

nodes.label: Memoization
nodes.summary: A cache is sound only when its key represents all output-relevant dependencies. Hidden mutable inputs break argument-only memoization.

nodes.label: Least recently used eviction
nodes.summary: Retain recently accessed entries subject to a capacity. Recency is a policy, not evidence quality or correctness.

nodes.label: Bounded FIFO eviction
nodes.summary: The supplied persistent result cache removes the oldest-written entries after 128 records. It is explicitly FIFO rather than LRU.

nodes.label: Time-to-live
nodes.summary: TTL limits reuse duration but cannot by itself detect a changed source or revoked scope. Version and validity checks are still required.

nodes.label: Dependency invalidation
nodes.summary: Include every semantically relevant dependency in the key, including source-only changes and policy versions.

nodes.label: Provider prompt cache
nodes.summary: Model-service prefix reuse is different from knowledge retrieval and local result caching; actual provider telemetry is required.

nodes.label: Attention key-value cache
nodes.summary: Cached intermediate key/value tensors reduce repeated attention computation during inference; they are not an editable evidence graph.

nodes.label: Tokenization
nodes.summary: Normalize text, choose word boundaries, handle domain symbols, and record stopword policy. These choices change ranking.

nodes.label: Inverse document frequency
nodes.summary: Rare query terms receive greater discriminating weight in a chosen eligible corpus. Compute counts after scope filtering.

nodes.label: BM25 lexical ranking
nodes.summary: Combine term saturation, document length normalization, and corpus frequency into an interpretable lexical baseline.

nodes.label: Embedding similarity
nodes.summary: A learned vector can place semantically similar passages near each other; closeness alone does not certify a claim or authorization.

nodes.label: Cosine similarity
nodes.summary: Compare vector directions after accounting for nonzero norms. Different embedding models create different geometries.

nodes.label: Adjacency matrix
nodes.summary: Matrix A encodes weighted vertex relations; its orientation convention must match transition equations.

nodes.label: Degree and hub effects
nodes.summary: A high-degree node can dominate navigation even when it is generic. Source references and analogy links need deliberate treatment.

nodes.label: Graph Laplacian
nodes.summary: L=D-A encodes local differences for an undirected nonnegative weighted graph. It has a constant-vector nullspace on each component.

nodes.label: Discrete Dirichlet energy
nodes.summary: The quadratic form sums weighted differences between linked vertices. Interpreting it as physical energy needs physical units and a calibrated model.

nodes.label: Grounding and boundary conditions
nodes.summary: Pin boundary values or impose a compatible gauge before inverting a singular Laplacian. Uniqueness depends on connectedness and boundary placement.

nodes.label: Heat diffusion on graphs
nodes.summary: Matrix exponentials smooth an initial signal according to graph connectivity. Smoothing can erase distinctions that evidence needs.

nodes.label: Random walk transition
nodes.summary: Normalize outgoing nonnegative weights. A vertex with no outgoing weight needs an explicit dangling-node rule.

nodes.label: Personalized PageRank
nodes.summary: Restart toward query seeds while traversing the eligible graph. The stationary mass is a retrieval affinity, not truth probability.

nodes.label: Contraction and convergence
nodes.summary: For restart probability above zero, the transition update contracts in L1. A reported iteration limit does not imply convergence.

nodes.label: Reciprocal rank fusion
nodes.summary: Combine lexical and graph rankings without pretending their raw scores have the same scale. Report the chosen constants.

nodes.label: Diversity-aware selection
nodes.summary: Balance query relevance against repetition; this is an optimization choice whose effects need a task benchmark.

nodes.label: Bounded evidence packets
nodes.summary: Limit the evidence sent to a model while preserving source locators and caveats. Track omitted items rather than silently implying full coverage.

nodes.label: Explanation paths
nodes.summary: Show why a node was retrieved and the typed relations linking it to direct matches. A path explains selection, not causation.

nodes.label: Bounded breadth-first traversal
nodes.summary: Visited identities and depth/node caps let cyclic knowledge graphs be explored without infinite traversal.

nodes.label: Prerequisite DAG
nodes.summary: A learning plan uses only prerequisite relations. General knowledge graphs may cycle even when the execution plan must not.

nodes.label: Cycle detection
nodes.summary: Kahn's algorithm reports a failed topological ordering; its remaining vertices can include descendants of cycles.

nodes.label: Idempotent operations
nodes.summary: Repeating the same snapshot ingest has no new state effect. A repeated external action still needs a provider-supported idempotency contract.

nodes.label: Durable checkpoints
nodes.summary: Save an artifact and its identity at a meaningful boundary. A claimed checkpoint without a readable artifact is incomplete.

nodes.label: Research improvement loops
nodes.summary: Each round changes a model or implementation in response to a specific observed weakness. Repeating a search is not automatically progress.

nodes.label: Stopping criteria
nodes.summary: Stop when acceptance is met, a bound is reached, or a decisive missing record blocks further progress; preserve the remaining question.

nodes.label: Retrieval baselines
nodes.summary: Compare lexical-only, graph-only, and fused retrieval on fixed questions and relevance labels before claiming a gain.

nodes.label: Recall and precision
nodes.summary: Count supported relevant evidence, not just generated answer fluency. Explicitly define the denominator and judging procedure.

nodes.label: Ranking quality
nodes.summary: Discount lower-ranked relevant items and normalize by an ideal order when relevance grades are well defined.

nodes.label: Abstention
nodes.summary: Return a gap when the available evidence cannot answer the question. A populated graph is not a reason to fabricate a match.

nodes.label: Temporal update tests
nodes.summary: Test future facts, expiry boundaries, corrections, and historical queries rather than only static fact lookup.

nodes.label: Calibration versus confidence
nodes.summary: A probability is calibrated only against outcomes with a defined evaluation population. Retrieval scores are not calibrated confidence.

nodes.label: Evaluation leakage
nodes.summary: Separate corpus preparation, answer labels, parameter tuning, and final evaluation. Duplicated sources are not independent confirmation.

nodes.label: Episodic memory
nodes.summary: In software, an episode can be an immutable observation or completed action; the biological notion involves richer behavioral and neural phenomena.

nodes.label: Semantic memory
nodes.summary: Curated concepts compress experience into reusable knowledge. Preserve links back to observations to detect errors introduced by compression.

nodes.label: Replay and consolidation
nodes.summary: Software can revisit cases and regression tests to consolidate a rule. This is a design analogy, not a demonstration of neural replay.

nodes.label: Hebbian associations
nodes.summary: Coactivation can strengthen a model connection, but cooccurrence alone is not evidence of cause, agreement, or truth.

nodes.label: Hopfield associative memory
nodes.summary: Under symmetric weights and asynchronous binary updates, a Lyapunov function can decrease toward stable states.

nodes.label: Attention-based association
nodes.summary: Attention mixes value vectors using query-key compatibility; particular modern Hopfield models establish a precise mathematical connection.

nodes.label: Forgetting and retention
nodes.summary: A decaying retrieval priority is a software policy. It must not delete durable evidence or imitate a universal human forgetting law.

nodes.label: Obsidian-compatible notes
nodes.summary: Export stable concept notes with typed link descriptions, sources, status, and formulas. Native links alone carry no theorem-verification status.

nodes.label: Foam in VS Code
nodes.summary: An editor-centered knowledge workflow can reuse portable Markdown notes and backlinks.

nodes.label: Logseq linked blocks
nodes.summary: Block-focused navigation provides another authoring granularity; retain explicit IDs during interchange.

nodes.label: Graphiti temporal graph
nodes.summary: A candidate external implementation for evolving relational memories, requiring its own deployment, licenses, and benchmark checks.

nodes.label: GraphRAG and global synthesis
nodes.summary: Community-level organization can help corpus-wide questions, but synthesis must remain auditable against original passages.

nodes.label: HippoRAG associative retrieval
nodes.summary: Personalized diffusion retrieves connected passages seeded by the question; the atlas uses a smaller deterministic graph baseline.

nodes.label: GraphRAG Zero
nodes.summary: A November 2026 provider research announcement describes retrieval built from embedding geometry with optional reasoning extensions.

nodes.label: Hindsight memory operations
nodes.summary: Study separation of retaining observations, recalling evidence, and reflecting; test each operation independently.

nodes.label: Mem0 consolidation
nodes.summary: Study selective memory extraction with revision and benchmark controls; product claims require exact configurations.

nodes.label: MemGPT memory tiers
nodes.summary: Treat active context as a scarce resource and durable evidence as an external store with explicit read/write operations.

nodes.label: Donna evidence handoff
nodes.summary: Give the assistant a bounded public evidence packet alongside separately authorized company knowledge. Do not infer a new access grant.

nodes.label: Skill memory workflow
nodes.summary: Before revisiting a problem, inspect relevant source-linked concepts, past decisions, unresolved objections, and versioned artifacts.

nodes.label: Repository knowledge graph
nodes.summary: Connect repo, commit, code path, test, source claim, and artifact with exact typed edges and distinct publication states.

nodes.label: Independent criticism
nodes.summary: A critic checks original evidence and assumptions, then identifies a concrete falsifier or repair. Agent agreement is not source independence.

nodes.label: Publication receipts
nodes.summary: A local commit, remote tree, workflow result, and live page are separate observations. Record each accurately.

nodes.label: Physics-to-memory operator bridges
nodes.summary: Laplacians, diffusion, oscillation, and energy functions can share mathematics while representing different physical or computational systems.

nodes.label: Spectral graph modes
nodes.summary: Eigenvectors form graph signal modes; eigenvalues become physical frequencies only after an explicit dynamical model and units.

nodes.label: Spin models and associative networks
nodes.summary: Some associative models resemble spin Hamiltonians mathematically; a software weight is not a measured magnetic coupling.

nodes.label: Association versus causation
nodes.summary: Graph adjacency is not a causal inference. Intervention, design assumptions, and competing explanations determine causal claims.

nodes.label: Lossy summary compression
nodes.summary: Summaries discard detail; preserve originals by pointer and maintain the ability to reopen source sections.

nodes.label: Information entropy
nodes.summary: Quantify uncertainty of a specified probability distribution. Entropy is not a substitute for epistemic quality or semantic understanding.

nodes.label: Cost and latency accounting
nodes.summary: Separate wall-clock time, local compute, provider tokens, and billable money. Report measured receipts, not inferred savings.

nodes.label: Question-led knowledge growth
nodes.summary: Store what would change the conclusion, prerequisites for answering it, and the next decisive source or experiment.

nodes.label: Propositions and quantifiers
nodes.summary: A quantifier fixes the universe and the order in which choices may depend on one another.

nodes.label: Sets, relations and functions
nodes.summary: Functions require a domain, codomain and unambiguous output; relations need not be functions.

nodes.label: Induction and recursion
nodes.summary: A base case and a justified successor step establish an infinite family without checking every case.

nodes.label: Proof obligations and counterexamples
nodes.summary: A theorem combines hypotheses, conclusion and a derivation; a single admissible counterexample defeats a universal claim.

nodes.label: Dependent types and proof terms
nodes.summary: Propositions can be represented as types and proofs as terms checked by a small kernel.

nodes.label: Axiom and dependency audit
nodes.summary: A proved proposition remains conditional on its actual axioms and dependency statements.

nodes.label: Equations and reversible transformations
nodes.summary: Division and squaring require domain checks to avoid dropping or adding solutions.

nodes.label: Polynomials and factorization
nodes.summary: Polynomial structure permits identities, roots and exact arithmetic independent of floating-point approximations.

nodes.label: Complex numbers and phase
nodes.summary: A complex number combines two real coordinates; multiplication combines scale and angle.

nodes.label: Exponentials and logarithms
nodes.summary: Logarithms turn multiplication into addition only on the selected domain and branch.

nodes.label: Dimensions and nondimensionalization
nodes.summary: Every additive term must share dimensions; a nondimensional variable is a ratio to a declared scale.

nodes.label: Groups and symmetry
nodes.summary: A group records reversible composition, identity and inverses without assuming commutativity.

nodes.label: Rings, ideals and quotients
nodes.summary: Rings combine addition and multiplication; ideals specify which expressions become equal in a quotient.

nodes.label: Fields and extensions
nodes.summary: A field permits division by nonzero elements; extensions add algebraic or transcendental elements.

nodes.label: Galois correspondence
nodes.summary: For finite Galois extensions, subfields and symmetry subgroups correspond in reverse inclusion.

nodes.label: Linear representations
nodes.summary: A representation turns group composition into matrix multiplication.

nodes.label: Lie groups and Lie algebras
nodes.summary: Infinitesimal generators organize local continuous symmetries and gauge theory.

nodes.label: Commutative algebra
nodes.summary: Localization and prime ideals connect polynomial equations with geometric spaces.

nodes.label: Vector spaces and linear maps
nodes.summary: Linearity means preserving addition and scalar multiplication; coordinates are a choice, not the object.

nodes.label: Basis and dimension
nodes.summary: A basis gives unique finite coordinate expansions; dimension counts independent directions.

nodes.label: Rank and nullspace
nodes.summary: The nullspace identifies invisible directions and prevents unjustified inversion.

nodes.label: Inner products and norms
nodes.summary: An inner product defines lengths and angles, with a conjugate transpose over complex scalars.

nodes.label: Determinants and orientation
nodes.summary: The determinant measures signed volume scaling of a square linear map.

nodes.label: Eigenvalues and spectral theorem
nodes.summary: Self-adjoint operators have orthogonal modes; arbitrary matrices need not diagonalize.

nodes.label: Singular value decomposition
nodes.summary: SVD separates input directions, gains and output directions for rectangular matrices.

nodes.label: Pseudoinverse and identifiable subspaces
nodes.summary: The pseudoinverse chooses a least-squares solution; it cannot recover an unobserved nullspace.

nodes.label: Least squares and projection
nodes.summary: Projection minimizes squared error under an explicitly chosen norm.

nodes.label: PCA and low-rank compression
nodes.summary: PCA captures variance directions, which need not be semantic or causal directions.

nodes.label: Tensors and multilinear maps
nodes.summary: Tensor rank, matrix rank and the number of stored entries describe different properties.

nodes.label: Condition numbers
nodes.summary: A stable algorithm cannot remove poor conditioning inherent in the mathematical problem.

nodes.label: Limits and continuity
nodes.summary: A limit describes controlled approach; sampled agreement does not establish continuity.

nodes.label: Derivatives and linearization
nodes.summary: The derivative is the local best linear approximation where it exists.

nodes.label: Taylor approximation and remainder
nodes.summary: A polynomial approximation becomes informative only with a bound on its remainder.

nodes.label: Integration and accumulation
nodes.summary: Integration accumulates quantities under a declared measure, domain and convergence condition.

nodes.label: Chain rule and automatic differentiation
nodes.summary: Derivative information propagates through function composition; branch behavior matters.

nodes.label: Jacobians and changes of variables
nodes.summary: The determinant of a coordinate derivative converts local volume elements.

nodes.label: Gradient, divergence and curl
nodes.summary: These operators depend on geometry and encode local change, flux and circulation.

nodes.label: Divergence theorem
nodes.summary: Boundary flux equals integrated interior divergence under regularity and orientation conditions.

nodes.label: Stokes theorem
nodes.summary: The differential-form theorem unifies several boundary-to-interior identities.

nodes.label: Calculus of variations
nodes.summary: Stationarity of a functional produces equations plus boundary conditions, not automatically a minimum.

nodes.label: Measure and integration
nodes.summary: A measure assigns consistent sizes; null sets and almost-everywhere statements differ from pointwise claims.

nodes.label: Banach and Hilbert spaces
nodes.summary: Completeness permits limits of approximations; Hilbert structure also supplies orthogonal projections.

nodes.label: Bounded and unbounded operators
nodes.summary: An unbounded operator is specified by its domain as well as its algebraic expression.

nodes.label: Holomorphic functions
nodes.summary: Complex differentiability imposes stronger constraints than real differentiability.

nodes.label: Fourier transforms and distributions
nodes.summary: Global frequency coordinates require a convention and a function or distribution class.

nodes.label: Sobolev spaces and weak derivatives
nodes.summary: Weak derivatives extend differential equations to functions without classical smoothness.

nodes.label: Boundary and initial value problems
nodes.summary: A differential equation needs data, solution class and a uniqueness/stability question.

nodes.label: Heat flow and smoothing
nodes.summary: Diffusion damps high-frequency modes, while backward reconstruction can be ill-conditioned.

nodes.label: Wave propagation
nodes.summary: Wave equations carry finite-speed propagation under appropriate local coefficients.

nodes.label: Weak solutions and variational formulations
nodes.summary: Testing against smooth functions changes the solution class and requires explicit energy and uniqueness conditions.

nodes.label: Distributions and Green functions
nodes.summary: A delta is a linear functional on test functions, not an ordinary infinitely high function.

nodes.label: Euclidean geometry and metric
nodes.summary: Metric information must be distinguished from a coordinate drawing.

nodes.label: Manifolds and charts
nodes.summary: A manifold is locally Euclidean; one chart rarely describes its entire topology.

nodes.label: Tangent spaces and differential forms
nodes.summary: Tangents represent velocities; cotangents act on them to give scalar measurements.

nodes.label: Riemannian and Lorentzian metrics
nodes.summary: A metric measures lengths or intervals and controls index raising and lowering.

nodes.label: Connections and covariant derivatives
nodes.summary: A connection compares vectors at nearby points; coordinate derivatives alone do not transform correctly.

nodes.label: Curvature and holonomy
nodes.summary: Curvature measures failure of local transport around infinitesimal loops to commute.

nodes.label: Laplace–Beltrami operator
nodes.summary: The Laplacian changes with the metric and volume element.

nodes.label: Geodesics and variational paths
nodes.summary: A geodesic is locally stationary for geometric length or energy and need not be globally shortest.

nodes.label: Topological spaces and continuity
nodes.summary: Topology records neighborhoods and continuity without requiring lengths.

nodes.label: Homotopy and fundamental group
nodes.summary: Continuous loop deformation is stronger than mere connectivity in a drawing.

nodes.label: Simplicial and cell complexes
nodes.summary: Higher-dimensional cells fill some graph cycles, changing which loops represent holes.

nodes.label: Homology and boundary maps
nodes.summary: Cycles modulo boundaries distinguish persistent holes from locally filled cycles.

nodes.label: Cohomology and dual observables
nodes.summary: Cohomology evaluates and combines global information carried by local data.

nodes.label: Persistent homology
nodes.summary: Persistence tracks features across a scale parameter, not proof of their physical meaning.

nodes.label: Hodge theory
nodes.summary: On suitable manifolds harmonic representatives connect PDEs with topological classes.

nodes.label: Graphs, multigraphs and typed edges
nodes.summary: Edge direction and type are part of the model; spatial proximity is not an edge.

nodes.label: Adjacency and walk counts
nodes.summary: Matrix powers count walks with multiplicity, including repeats.

nodes.label: Incidence matrices and conservation
nodes.summary: A signed incidence matrix expresses how edge flows enter and leave vertices.

nodes.label: Graph Laplacians
nodes.summary: A Laplacian is a positive semidefinite quadratic energy on an undirected weighted graph.

nodes.label: Normalized graph Laplacian
nodes.summary: Degree normalization controls the geometry used to compare cuts and random-walk mixing.

nodes.label: Graph diffusion and heat kernels
nodes.summary: Diffusion smooths a signal across encoded edges and loses high-frequency distinctions.

nodes.label: Effective resistance
nodes.summary: Resistance measures redundancy of paths under conductance assumptions.

nodes.label: Conductance and spectral gaps
nodes.summary: A small bottleneck limits mixing and connects combinatorial cuts to eigenvalues.

nodes.label: Shortest paths and dynamic programming
nodes.summary: Shortest cost depends on edge weights and constraints; it is not strongest evidence.

nodes.label: DAGs and topological ordering
nodes.summary: A DAG permits prerequisite order; detected cycles need interpretation, not silent truncation.

nodes.label: Strongly connected components
nodes.summary: Collapsing directed feedback components produces a DAG without pretending the loops disappeared.

nodes.label: Counting, extremal sets and Ramsey theory
nodes.summary: Existence, constructive algorithms and optimal bounds are distinct questions.

nodes.label: Probability spaces and events
nodes.summary: Probabilities are conditional on a chosen experiment and model, not inherent truth scores.

nodes.label: Random variables and distributions
nodes.summary: A random variable is a measurable function, not a sample or a probability density itself.

nodes.label: Bayesian conditioning
nodes.summary: Updating needs likelihoods and a denominator that can be nonzero; repeated evidence may be dependent.

nodes.label: Covariance and correlation
nodes.summary: Zero covariance alone does not imply independence.

nodes.label: Gaussian models
nodes.summary: A covariance matrix must be positive semidefinite; a density needs nonsingular covariance.

nodes.label: Concentration inequalities
nodes.summary: Bounds depend on independence or other assumptions and cannot be reused after arbitrary selection.

nodes.label: Markov chains and stationarity
nodes.summary: The Markov property discards history only after choosing a sufficient state.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo and sampling error
nodes.summary: Variance and dependence determine effective precision; more repeated samples need not mean more independent information.

nodes.label: Causal models and interventions
nodes.summary: Association graphs do not establish intervention effects without identification assumptions.

nodes.label: Shannon entropy
nodes.summary: Entropy quantifies a distribution's uncertainty in specified log units.

nodes.label: Relative entropy and information gain
nodes.summary: KL is directional and can be infinite when support is missing.

nodes.label: Mutual information
nodes.summary: Information shared statistically is not the same as a causal mechanism.

nodes.label: Regularization and inverse problems
nodes.summary: A penalty stabilizes solutions by introducing a modeling preference.

nodes.label: Generalization and evaluation
nodes.summary: Performance must be measured on the intended distribution with contamination controls.

nodes.label: Embeddings and metric learning
nodes.summary: A learned vector geometry is an approximation tied to model, objective and training data.

nodes.label: Floating-point arithmetic
nodes.summary: Finite precision makes operation order important and can destroy naive cancellation.

nodes.label: Root finding and Newton iteration
nodes.summary: Newton is locally powerful but can diverge or converge to an unintended root.

nodes.label: Convex and nonconvex optimization
nodes.summary: The feasible domain and curvature determine whether a stationary point is globally optimal.

nodes.label: Gradient descent and step sizes
nodes.summary: Step size and smoothness control descent; a large learning rate can cause oscillation.

nodes.label: Lagrange duality and KKT conditions
nodes.summary: Dual variables can certify bounds, with constraint qualifications needed for equality of optima.

nodes.label: Conjugate gradients and preconditioning
nodes.summary: CG exploits SPD structure; preconditioning changes the geometry of convergence.

nodes.label: Finite differences
nodes.summary: Consistency must be paired with stability and boundary treatment.

nodes.label: Finite elements and weak forms
nodes.summary: Basis functions approximate a variational solution while respecting boundary constraints.

nodes.label: Numerical quadrature
nodes.summary: Smoothness and sampling placement determine error; highly oscillatory integrands need specialized treatment.

nodes.label: Contractions and fixed points
nodes.summary: A contraction supplies existence, uniqueness and a quantitative stopping certificate.

nodes.label: Computational complexity and reductions
nodes.summary: A theorem about Turing machines, word RAM or arithmetic circuits must retain that model.

nodes.label: Linear programming
nodes.summary: LP optimality and algorithmic complexity are separate properties.

nodes.label: Primes and unique factorization
nodes.summary: Prime factorization translates multiplication into exponents, while computation can remain hard.

nodes.label: Zeta and L-functions
nodes.summary: Analytic continuation and zero locations connect complex analysis with arithmetic.

nodes.label: Elliptic curves
nodes.summary: A nonsingular genus-one curve with a chosen point admits a geometric group law.

nodes.label: Modular and automorphic forms
nodes.summary: Automorphy constrains analytic functions under arithmetic group actions.

nodes.label: Schemes and sheaves
nodes.summary: Local rings and gluing preserve algebraic structure that point sets alone lose.

nodes.label: Langlands correspondences
nodes.summary: Different Langlands programs require different precise statements and are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: Categories and composition
nodes.summary: Objects, morphisms and their lawful composition give a language for comparisons across subjects.

nodes.label: Functors and structure preservation
nodes.summary: A functor must preserve identities and composition, not merely pair similar-looking objects.

nodes.label: Natural transformations
nodes.summary: Naturality requires a commuting relation for every relevant morphism.

nodes.label: Universal properties and limits
nodes.summary: A construction is characterized by how all admissible maps factor through it.

nodes.label: Yoneda and representability
nodes.summary: An object is characterized, up to isomorphism, by its relationships expressed through hom-functors.

nodes.label: All mathematical problems have been solved
nodes.summary: No. A catalogue or benchmark cannot establish universal mathematical solvability.

nodes.label: Gemini Deep Think: IMO 2025 gold-standard performance
nodes.summary: Five of six competition problems, 35 points, reported gold-medal standard.

nodes.label: Planar unit distances: polynomial construction improvement
nodes.summary: There is δ>0 and infinitely many n for which ν(n)≥n^(1+δ).

nodes.label: OpenAI ten-advance collection
nodes.summary: A collection covers discrete geometry, coding, group/operator problems and complexity.

nodes.label: Claude-assisted simple critical-line zeta-zero proportion
nodes.summary: The paper gives a simple critical-line zero proportion exceeding two thirds; a window calculation gives 0.6725.

nodes.label: Fermat’s Last Theorem: large Lean formalization
nodes.summary: For natural n≥3 and positive natural a,b,c, a^n+b^n≠c^n.

nodes.label: Forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes breakdown
nodes.summary: For every ν>0, smooth compact forcing produces zero-initial-data smooth flow on [0,1) with bounded L² energy and unbounded L∞ near time 1.

nodes.label: Separate unforced Euler singularity artifact
nodes.summary: The repository separately formalizes finite-time breakdown for unforced three-dimensional Euler.

nodes.label: Navier–Stokes prose/formal translation criticism
nodes.summary: The critique identifies differences between prose and formalized intermediate estimates.

nodes.label: OpenAI mathematics catalogue: exact metadata census
nodes.summary: The pinned CONTENTS file yields 730 manuscript links grouped into 375 result families.

nodes.summary: The release history withdraws three Hodge-related manuscripts after a stabilization-trace sign error.

nodes.summary: The paper states bounded-integer 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and APSP in O(n^2.9995), rounded exponents.

nodes.summary: A deterministic counting 3-SAT algorithm is claimed with time 2^{O(n log log n / sqrt(log n))}.

nodes.label: OpenAI fixed-width counting-SAT subexponential claim
nodes.summary: Reports deterministic subexponential-time, polynomial-space counting of k-CNF assignments for fixed k.

nodes.label: OpenAI local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation
nodes.summary: Announces local smoothing in spatial dimensions at least two with harmonic-analysis consequences.

nodes.summary: The working group reports a Wilson-lattice scaling-limit construction satisfying Wightman axioms.

nodes.label: OpenAI November 24 complexity and polytope additions
nodes.summary: Nine new manuscripts in families 379–380 include tensor/circuit claims, multiplication exponents, sunflowers and linear programming.

nodes.summary: The released formal proof is certified to match Mathlib’s RiemannHypothesis proposition.

nodes.summary: MIT reports independently checked critical-strip zero statements for Dirichlet L-functions across all positive moduli and all characters, including the primitive-character formulation.

nodes.summary: The available challenge declarations derive breakdown conditional on a bounded periodic similarity profile/certificate.

nodes.label: Wang–Zahl three-dimensional Kakeya theorem
nodes.summary: Every Kakeya set in R³ has full Hausdorff and Minkowski dimension.

nodes.label: Categorical unramified geometric Langlands project
nodes.summary: A five-paper project proves the categorical unramified geometric Langlands conjecture in its stated setting.

nodes.label: Electric charge
nodes.summary: Signed conserved source quantity; distributions require specifying point, surface or volume idealization.

nodes.label: Electric field
nodes.summary: Force per test charge; a vector field with units V/m, not an energy or voltage.

nodes.label: Coulomb interaction
nodes.summary: Inverse-square static interaction in homogeneous vacuum with a point-charge idealization.

nodes.label: Electrostatic superposition
nodes.summary: Linear source-to-field mapping for prescribed charge and linear media; material self-consistency can be nonlinear.

nodes.label: Scalar potential

nodes.label: Adjacency and weighted degree
nodes.summary: Place each edge weight at its row and column. Summing a row counts outgoing weight; this is bookkeeping, not an inferred relationship.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></munder><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>diag</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
A_{ij}=w_{ij},\qquad d_i=\sum_j A_{ij},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Declare whether rows encode outgoing edges.
Weights are nonnegative for a random-walk interpretation.
nodes.example: A unit-weight path of three vertices has degrees (1,2,1) when represented as an undirected graph.
limitations: A directed graph generally has different incoming and outgoing degree.

nodes.label: Combinatorial Laplacian
nodes.summary: Row i acts on x by summing w_ij(x_i-x_j); a constant signal produces zero differences.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>L</mi><mn>𝟏</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
L=D-A,\qquad L\mathbf 1=0
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Undirected graph with nonnegative weights.
nodes.example: For the three-vertex path, L=[[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]], with eigenvalues 0,1,3.
limitations: L is singular on each connected component. A directed version needs a separately stated convention.

nodes.label: Dirichlet quadratic form
nodes.summary: Expand the square and collect the two degree terms; symmetry turns both into x^TDx, while cross terms give twice x^TAx.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>L</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
x^TLx=\frac12\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Symmetric nonnegative weights.
The double sum counts both orientations.
nodes.example: For path values (1,0,-1), the two undirected edge differences both equal 1, hence x^TLx=2.
limitations: Units are weight times signal squared. Calling this physical energy requires an additional physical model.

nodes.label: Grounded Poisson problem
nodes.summary: Partition Lu=b into interior and boundary blocks; move the known boundary term to the right. The grounded interior operator is positive definite under the connectivity assumption.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>I</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
L_{II}u_I=b_I-L_{IB}u_B
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Every connected component of interior vertices reaches a fixed boundary.
Boundary values and compatible source units are specified.
nodes.example: For a three-point path with endpoints 1 and 0 and no interior source, 2u_middle=1, so u_middle=0.5.
limitations: Without grounding or compatibility constraints, inversion is not unique or may be inconsistent.

nodes.label: Graph heat flow
nodes.summary: Diagonalize L=UΛUᵀ; each mode obeys a scalar decay equation with solution exp(-κλt).
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><mi>κ</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>κ</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\frac{dx}{dt}=-\kappa Lx,\qquad x(t)=e^{-\kappa Lt}x(0)
</annotation></semantics></math>

variables.unit: inverse time when L is dimensionless

assumptions: Fixed symmetric nonnegative graph.
Linear dynamics.
nodes.example: A mode with λ=2 and κ=1 s^-1 decays to exp(-2)≈0.1353 of its initial amplitude after 1 s.
limitations: Smoothing can remove a rare but essential distinction. A diffusion parameter is not automatically a biological timescale.

nodes.label: Graph wave modes
nodes.summary: Project onto each eigenvector to obtain an independent harmonic-oscillator equation.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mover><mi>x</mi><mo accent="true">̈</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>L</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><msqrt><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\ddot x+\omega_0^2 Lx=0,\qquad \omega_k=\omega_0\sqrt{\lambda_k}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A physical or simulated second-order dynamical law is explicitly posited.
L is positive semidefinite.
nodes.example: For path eigenvalue λ=3 and ω0=2 rad/s, the mode has ω=2√3 rad/s.
limitations: A note graph alone has no clock, mass, stiffness, or measured acoustic frequency.

nodes.label: Row-stochastic transition
nodes.summary: Divide each outgoing weight by the row sum, producing total probability one.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mi>/</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="1.0em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
P_{ij}=A_{ij}/d_i\quad(d_i>0)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Nonnegative weights.
A separate redistribution rule is defined for dangling rows.
nodes.example: Weights (2,1) yield outgoing probabilities (2/3,1/3).
limitations: Negative relations cannot be inserted as negative probabilities. Keep contradicts as a separate semantic channel.

nodes.label: Personalized PageRank
nodes.summary: At a fixed point, collect terms in p. Invertibility follows because the spectral radius of αPᵀ is below one. The Neumann series sums walks of every length with geometric damping.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>p</mi><mo>*</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>−</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
p_{t+1}=\alpha P^Tp_t+(1-\alpha)s,\qquad p_*=(1-\alpha)(I-\alpha P^T)^{-1}s
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: P is row-stochastic after dangling-node handling.
s is nonnegative and sums to one.
nodes.example: For two alternating vertices, seed (1,0), and α=0.85, p=(1/1.85,0.85/1.85)≈(0.54054,0.45946).
limitations: Stationary mass measures graph affinity. It is not probability that a scientific claim is correct.

nodes.label: PageRank residual bound
nodes.summary: The future increments are bounded by a geometric sequence. Sum their norms to bound the distance from the current iterate to the limit.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mo>*</mo></msub><msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\lVert p_t-p_*\rVert_1\leq\frac{\lVert p_{t+1}-p_t\rVert_1}{1-\alpha}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Stochastic transition with 0≤α<1.
nodes.example: At α=0.85 and residual 10^-10, this bound is at most 6.67×10^-10.
limitations: An iteration cap can stop before this bound is small; record residual and iteration count.

nodes.label: Positive inverse document frequency
nodes.summary: The smoothed frequency ratio increases as a term becomes rarer; the outer 1 keeps this common BM25 variant positive.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>idf</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>log</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{idf}(t)=\log\left(1+\frac{N-n_t+0.5}{n_t+0.5}\right)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Compute statistics only over authorized active documents.
Natural logarithm is used.
limitations: Changing the corpus changes IDF. It does not measure the truth or novelty of a claim.

nodes.label: BM25 retrieval score
nodes.summary: The fractional term grows with term frequency but saturates. Length normalization changes the denominator according to relative document length.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></munder><mo>idf</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mover><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo accent="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
S(q,d)=\sum_{t\in q}\operatorname{idf}(t)\frac{f_{t,d}(k_1+1)}{f_{t,d}+k_1(1-b+b|d|/\overline{|d|})}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Chosen tokenizer and document construction are fixed.
Implementation uses k1=1.2 and b=0.75.
nodes.example: If a document has average length and term frequency 1, the fraction equals 1, leaving exactly its IDF contribution.
limitations: These constants are a baseline, not optimized for this corpus. Repeated labels receive deliberate extra weight.

nodes.label: Cosine similarity
nodes.summary: Divide the inner product by magnitudes to isolate the angle between vectors.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>sim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">∥</mo><mi>x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">∥</mo><mi>y</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{sim}(x,y)=\frac{x^Ty}{\lVert x\rVert_2\lVert y\rVert_2}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Both vectors have nonzero norm.
Both come from the same compatible embedding space.
nodes.example: Vectors (1,0) and (1,1) have cosine 1/√2≈0.7071.
limitations: High similarity can link incompatible claims. Embeddings are a documented future adapter, not used in the implemented baseline.

nodes.label: Weighted reciprocal rank fusion
nodes.summary: Replace incomparable raw scores with reciprocal rank contributions, then sum channels. The implemented weights are 1 for lexical and 0.7 for graph, with c=60.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></munder><mfrac><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
R(d)=\sum_j\frac{w_j}{c+r_j(d)}
</annotation></semantics></math>

variables.meaning: one-based rank in retrieval channel j

assumptions: Missing items contribute zero.
Ranks start at one.
nodes.example: An item ranked first in both channels scores 1.7/61≈0.027869; this is a ranking score, not 2.79% confidence.
limitations: Weights need held-out evaluation; a dense graph can still introduce irrelevant linked items.

nodes.label: Relevance and redundancy tradeoff
nodes.summary: A greedy step rewards query relevance and penalizes similarity to selected evidence. This defines an engineering policy rather than a general optimum.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mo>*</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>arg</mo><munder><mo>max</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mi>λ</mi><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><munder><mo>max</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></munder><mo>sim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
d_* =\arg\max_{d\notin S}\left[\lambda\,r(q,d)-(1-\lambda)\max_{s\in S}\operatorname{sim}(d,s)\right]
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Comparable, bounded relevance and similarity scales.
nodes.example: At λ=0.7, relevance 0.9 and maximum redundancy 0.8 give 0.63-0.24=0.39.
limitations: Not implemented in the initial retrieval core; retained as an evaluable extension.

nodes.label: Shannon entropy of a declared distribution
nodes.summary: Weight each outcome's self-information by its probability. This measures uncertainty of that distribution, not semantic wisdom.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>x</mi></munder><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>log</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
H(X)=-\sum_x p(x)\log_2 p(x)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A normalized distribution and outcome space are specified.
Use 0 log 0=0 by continuity.
nodes.example: A fair binary variable has entropy 1 bit; a deterministic variable has entropy 0.
limitations: Low entropy may reflect unwarranted certainty. It is not evidence quality.
taxonomy_path: Shannon entropy of a declared distribution

nodes.label: Expected local cache latency
nodes.summary: Condition total expectation on the two disjoint cases. If miss cost is measured after lookup instead, add the lookup cost separately.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\mathbb{E}[T]=hT_{\mathrm{hit}}+(1-h)T_{\mathrm{miss}}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Hit and miss latencies include the same measurement boundaries.
Workload hit fraction is representative.
nodes.example: With h=0.8, a 2 ms hit and a 40 ms complete miss, E[T]=9.6 ms.
limitations: Mean latency does not describe p95 or concurrent queueing. These numbers are an example, not a measured product result.

nodes.label: Two-level average memory access time
nodes.summary: Expand a decision tree: every request pays T1, m1 of requests pay T2, and m1m2 pay T3.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
T_{\mathrm{avg}}=T_1+m_1(T_2+m_2T_3)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Each lower-tier cost is incurred only after an upper-tier miss.
Use incremental costs, not complete inclusive timings.
nodes.example: T1=1, T2=10, T3=100, m1=0.1, m2=0.2 yield 4 time units.
limitations: Correlated workloads and overlapping asynchronous fetches require a different timing model.

nodes.label: Poisson-update freshness model
nodes.summary: The no-update probability is the zero-count Poisson mass exp(-λt); subtract from one.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>Pr</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mrow><mtext mathvariant="normal">at least one update in </mtext><mspace width="0.333em"></mspace></mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>λ</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\Pr(\text{at least one update in }t)=1-e^{-\lambda t}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Updates are modeled as a homogeneous Poisson process.
nodes.example: With λ=1 update/hour and age 0.5 hour, probability of an intervening update is about 0.3935.
limitations: Real source changes are often bursty or adversarial. Versioned invalidation is stronger than this heuristic.

nodes.label: Fully associative LRU hit condition
nodes.summary: Every distinct intervening item moves the reused entry down one position in the recency stack; capacity C retains the first C positions.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext mathvariant="normal">hit at capacity </mtext><mspace width="0.333em"></mspace></mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⇔</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\text{hit at capacity }C\iff d_{\mathrm{reuse}}<C
</annotation></semantics></math>

variables.meaning: distinct other items since previous access

assumptions: Fully associative LRU.
Uniform-sized entries and no external invalidation.
First use has infinite reuse distance.
nodes.example: Trace A,B,C,A has reuse distance 2 for the last A: it misses at capacity 2 and hits at capacity 3.
limitations: The supplied persisted cache is FIFO and does not claim this LRU guarantee.

nodes.label: Complete cache dependency key
nodes.summary: Treat the result as a function of declared inputs. Equal keys justify reuse only insofar as the serialization captures every relevant input.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>SHA256</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mo>canon</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
K=\operatorname{SHA256}(\operatorname{canon}(q,V,A,S,P,T,\theta))
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Canonical serialization is deterministic.
All output-relevant dependencies are included.
Cryptographic hash collisions are assumed negligible.
nodes.example: A source URL correction changes V and therefore the key even when the node summary text is unchanged.
limitations: A digest does not validate the source, authenticate a caller, or prove semantic equivalence.

nodes.label: Evidence selection under a byte budget
nodes.summary: A constrained subset problem formalizes why not every retrieved item fits. The implementation greedily tries ranked packets and checks actual UTF-8 bytes.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo>max</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">}</mo></mrow></munder><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mspace width="1.0em"></mspace><mtext mathvariant="normal">s.t.</mtext><mspace width="1.0em"></mspace><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\max_{z_i\in\{0,1\}}\sum_i u_i z_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\sum_i b_i z_i\le B
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Utilities and sizes are specified.
Independent additive utility is an approximation.
nodes.example: With sizes 6 and 5 and budget 5, only the second item fits, regardless of the first item's better rank.
limitations: Greedy rank order does not solve general knapsack optimally; correlated evidence requires nonadditive utility.
taxonomy_path: Evidence selection under a byte budget

nodes.label: Traversal complexity
nodes.summary: Each vertex enters the queue once and each relevant adjacency is examined a bounded number of times.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
T_{\mathrm{BFS}}=O(|V_r|+|E_r|),\qquad M=O(|V_r|)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Adjacency lists and a visited set.
Constant-time set operations are an average-case assumption.
nodes.example: In a cycle A→B→C→A, the visited set stops the fourth enqueue of A.
limitations: Building the eligible subgraph and adjacency has its own whole-graph cost; report that in end-to-end benchmarks.

nodes.label: DAG topological condition
nodes.summary: A finite acyclic directed graph has a zero-indegree vertex. A cycle leaves each of its vertices with an incoming edge, preventing complete elimination.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mo>Kahn</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo>⇔</mo><mi>G</mi><mrow><mspace width="0.333em"></mspace><mtext mathvariant="normal"> is a DAG</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
|\operatorname{Kahn}(G)|=|V|\iff G\text{ is a DAG}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Remove vertices of zero indegree and their outgoing edges.
nodes.example: A requires B and B requires A gives no valid topological order; C depending on A can also remain blocked.
limitations: Remaining blocked vertices are not necessarily all members of a cycle.

nodes.label: Simple Hebbian weight construction
nodes.summary: Correlated components contribute positive weights and opposite components negative weights; summing patterns superposes their associations.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>P</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
W_{ij}=\frac1N\sum_{\mu=1}^{P}\xi_i^{(\mu)}\xi_j^{(\mu)},\qquad W_{ii}=0
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A specified binary-pattern associative model.
This is a theoretical rule, not a universal synaptic law.
nodes.example: For one pattern (1,-1), the off-diagonal weights are -1/2 under N=2 normalization.
limitations: Interference and spurious attractors occur. Coactivation does not imply causal evidence.

nodes.label: Binary Hopfield Lyapunov function
nodes.summary: If only state i changes, ΔE=-(s_i'−s_i)(Σ_j W_ij s_j−θ_i). Choosing the state aligned with the field makes this nonpositive.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>W</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
E(s)=-\frac12s^TWs+\theta^Ts
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: W=Wᵀ and diagonal zero.
Asynchronous single-unit updates align with the local field.
nodes.example: Two positively coupled units lower this function by agreeing rather than disagreeing, for zero thresholds.
limitations: Synchronous updates can oscillate. The function is not automatically a joule-valued physical energy.

nodes.label: Scaled dot-product attention
nodes.summary: Dot products give compatibility logits; scaling moderates their growth with dimension, softmax normalizes, and the resulting weights mix values.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>Attention</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>softmax</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>/</mi><msqrt><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\operatorname{softmax}(QK^T/\sqrt{d_k})V
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Matrix dimensions are compatible.
Softmax operates across available keys, with any mask explicitly stated.
nodes.example: For two equal unmasked logits, each value receives weight 1/2.
limitations: A KV cache stores intermediate tensors; it is different from external source-linked memory.

nodes.label: Exponential retrieval-priority heuristic
nodes.summary: Solve dw/dt=−w/τ. This defines a convenient recency prior; it is not fitted biological evidence.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
w(t)=w_0e^{-t/\tau}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A software prioritization rule is explicitly chosen.
nodes.example: After time τ, weight is w0/e≈0.3679w0.
limitations: Never let an arbitrary decay delete provenance or turn an established theorem false.

nodes.label: Evidence precision and recall
nodes.summary: Precision asks how much retrieved evidence is relevant; recall asks how much relevant evidence was found.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>Precision</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo>Recall</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{Precision}=\frac{|R\cap G|}{|R|},\qquad\operatorname{Recall}=\frac{|R\cap G|}{|G|}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Gold relevance and evidence units are specified.
Define behavior for empty denominators before evaluation.
nodes.example: Retrieving 5 items, 3 relevant, from 4 relevant items gives precision 0.6 and recall 0.75.
limitations: Gold labels can be incomplete; duplicate passages must not inflate independent support.

nodes.label: Discounted cumulative gain
nodes.summary: Higher-ranked relevant items contribute more. Divide by the best available ordering to normalize the score.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>DCG</mo><mi>@</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>log</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo>nDCG</mo><mi>@</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>DCG</mo><mi>@</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>/</mi><mo>IDCG</mo><mi>@</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{DCG}@k=\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{2^{rel_i}-1}{\log_2(i+1)},\qquad\operatorname{nDCG}@k=\operatorname{DCG}@k/\operatorname{IDCG}@k
</annotation></semantics></math>

variables.meaning: ideal score under the same labels

assumptions: Nonnegative relevance grades.
Define the all-zero relevance case.
nodes.example: For binary relevance (1,0,1), DCG@3=1+0+1/2=1.5.
limitations: Metric choice does not certify answer correctness or source trustworthiness.

nodes.label: Brier calibration score
nodes.summary: Use the squared error of probabilistic predictions and average over evaluated cases.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
B=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(p_i-y_i)^2
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A well-defined population of binary outcomes.
Predictions precede observed outcomes.
nodes.example: Predictions (0.8,0.2) for outcomes (1,0) have Brier score 0.04.
limitations: Graph ranks and RRF scores are not probabilities and must not be inserted directly as calibrated confidence.

nodes.label: Measured improvement in a fixed loop
nodes.summary: Evaluate both revisions on the same criterion, then subtract. This distinguishes observed progress from activity counts.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mtext mathvariant="normal">system</mtext><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mtext mathvariant="normal">system</mtext><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\Delta U_k=U(\text{system}_{k+1};D)-U(\text{system}_{k};D)
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: Hold evaluation data and judging procedure fixed within a comparison.
Track resource cost and regressions separately.
nodes.example: Recall increasing from 0.60 to 0.65 is a five-percentage-point change on that evaluation; it is not proof of universal improvement.
limitations: Repeated tuning on the same cases can overfit; retain held-out questions and report uncertainty.
taxonomy_path: Measured improvement in a fixed loop

nodes.label: Quadratic equation by completing the square
nodes.summary: Divide by a and move c/a. Adding (b/2a)² makes (x+b/2a)²=(b²−4ac)/(4a²). Taking both square roots and subtracting b/2a gives the formula. The division step excludes a=0, which must instead be treated as a linear or constant equation.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>−</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: a is nonzero.
Use real roots only when the discriminant is nonnegative; over complex numbers select both square roots.
nodes.example: For x²−5x+6=0 the discriminant is 1 and the roots are 2 and 3; substitution makes each residual zero.
limitations: Direct evaluation can lose precision when b and the square root nearly cancel; compute one root stably and obtain the other from their product c/a.
taxonomy_path: Quadratic equation by completing the square

nodes.label: Finite binomial theorem
nodes.summary: Expand the product of n copies of a+b. To obtain a term with k factors b, choose k of the n positions; there are binomial(n,k) choices. Commutation lets these products share one coefficient. This finite counting argument does not establish convergence of a generalized infinite binomial series.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0"><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
(a+b)^n=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nk a^{n-k}b^k
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: n is a nonnegative integer.
a and b commute.
nodes.example: For n=3 the coefficients 1,3,3,1 give (a+b)³=a³+3a²b+3ab²+b³.
limitations: For noncommuting matrices AB and BA differ; the scalar formula cannot be substituted blindly.

nodes.label: Complex exponential and phase
nodes.summary: Separate the absolutely convergent power series for exp(iθ) into even and odd powers. The even part is cosine and the odd part is i times sine. Multiplication of exponentials then yields angle-addition rules, showing why complex multiplication represents rotations.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>cos</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>sin</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: θ is real for the unit-circle interpretation.
nodes.example: At θ=π/2, the value is i. Multiplication by i maps the point 1 to i, a quarter turn.
limitations: A physical frequency in hertz must enter θ as 2πft; confusing cycles with radians changes results by 2π.

nodes.label: Rank–nullity and lost directions
nodes.summary: Choose a basis of the nullspace and extend it to a basis of the domain. The images of the additional vectors form a basis of the image. Therefore every input direction is either accounted for by an independent observable direction or contributes to the kernel dimension.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>rank</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>dim</mo><mo>ker</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mi>A</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
\operatorname{rank}A+\dim\ker A=n,\qquad A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m
</annotation></semantics></math>
assumptions: A is a finite-dimensional linear map.
nodes.example: A=[1 0] maps R² to R. Its rank is 1 and nullspace is {(0,t)}. Its sole returned singular value is positive, yet recovery of the second coordinate is impossible.
limitations: A rectangular SVD can list only positive returned singular values while omitting nullspace directions on the larger side.

nodes.label: Cauchy–Schwarz and cosine similarity
nodes.summary: For y≠0 minimize ||x−αy||² over α. Nonnegativity at the minimizer gives ||x||²−|〈x,y〉|²/||y||²≥0. In real Euclidean geometry the normalized dot product therefore lies in [−1,1] and can define an angle.
nodes.mathml:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">⟨</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">⟩</mo><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mo>,</mo><mspace width="2.0em"></mspace><mo>cos</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">∥</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">
|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\|y\|,\qquad \cos\theta=\frac{x^Ty}{\|x\|\|y\|}
</annotation></semantics></math>

variables.meaning: vectors in a real inner-product space

assumptions: The angle formula uses real nonzero vectors.
For complex spaces use the Hermitian inner product for the inequality.
nodes.example: x=(1,0), y=(1,1) have cosine 1/√2. x and 100x have cosine 1 even though their lengths differ by 100.
limitations: Similarity is undefined for a zero vector and is not a probability that two claims are true or equivalent.

nodes.label: Two-dimensional determinant and inverse
